pcs.pc_description: Review department-wise budgets and make amendments if required.
Regularly track actual performance against budgeted figures to forecast future financial trends.

Manage expenses carefully to ensure profitability by identifying and minimising waste.
Assess different revenue streams and find growth opportunities, such as pricing strategies or exploring new markets.

pcs.pc_description: Evaluate the transportation needs based on the type of goods to be delivered (e.g., perishable goods, heavy machinery, small packages) and determine the appropriate vehicle types (trucks, vans, specialised vehicles).
Work with procurement teams to acquire vehicles by researching and selecting the best vehicles based on cost, fuel efficiency, capacity, and maintenance needs.
Decide whether to lease or purchase vehicles based on financial considerations, such as cash flow, asset management, and long-term operational goals.
Implement a fleet management system or software to track maintenance schedules, service history, and vehicle conditions.
Train drivers on best safety practices, including handling cargo, safe driving techniques, and emergency procedures.
Ensure all vehicles undergo regular preventive maintenance to reduce breakdowns and extend vehicle lifespan. This includes oil changes, tyre rotations, brake inspections, etc.
Ensure that vehicles meet safety standards and regulatory requirements (e.g., DOT inspections, weight limits). Perform routine safety checks on tyres, brakes, lights, and other critical components.
Optimise vehicle routes to reduce fuel consumption, time, and overall operational costs.
Monitor how often each vehicle is used and ensure the fleet is being utilised to its full potential.
Avoid underutilised vehicles while preventing the overuse of others.
Make sure that vehicles carry full loads whenever possible, ensuring that deliveries are made efficiently.
Track driver behaviour (speeding, harsh braking, idling time) through GPS or telematics systems and address any performance issues to ensure safety and fuel efficiency.
Use fleet management software to track fuel usage and detect inefficiency (e.g., excessive idling and poor driving habits).
Continuously evaluate the total cost of ownership for each vehicle in the fleet, considering factors like fuel efficiency, maintenance, insurance, and depreciation.
Ensure that all vehicles meet local, national, and international regulations regarding weight, emissions, and roadworthiness (e.g., compliance with environmental standards and safety regulations).
Implement ELDs (Electronic Logging Devices) to monitor and enforce compliance with driver working hours and rest periods and ensure accurate reporting for regulatory compliance.
Use data collected from telematics and fleet management systems to make informed decisions about vehicle purchases, route planning, and driver management.
Implement a system to report and track accidents or incidents involving the fleet. Investigate the root causes and take corrective action to prevent future occurrences.
Track key performance indicators (KPIs) such as on-time deliveries, fuel efficiency, vehicle downtime, and cost per mile/km.
Implement green practices such as promoting fuel-efficient driving habits, reducing idling times, and exploring the use of alternative fuel vehicles (electric, hybrid, or compressed natural gas).
Monitor the fleet’s carbon footprint and take steps to reduce emissions, potentially integrating electric vehicles or hybrid options to reduce environmental impact.
Ensure that the fleet is compliant with environmental regulations regarding emissions and noise pollution.
